paragraphs: Here's what Samson's whole case comes down to, friend: "she is pleasing to my eyes." (Judges 14:3) That's the argument. I have picked dough by how pretty it looked in the bowl, and the oven told me the truth about it later. Eyes are great at starting things and terrible at finishing them.

But look at the side note the writer drops in. Samson's father and mother did not know this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines (Judges 14:4). So God's plan keeps moving even through a choice that begins with Samson's eyes. The Spirit of the LORD comes powerfully on him (Judges 14:6, 19), and still Samson ends up burning with anger and without his wife (Judges 14:19-20).

So here's the big idea, friend: God can carry out His purposes through anybody, and that is no reason to run on what looks good to you. Samson keeps secrets from his father and mother (Judges 14:6, 9), and then he gets pressed for seven days until he gives in (Judges 14:17). I'd rather bring my wants to the LORD before they take me down the road. And hang on to your apron, because this story is NOT over.
